predecessors.name: Kingdom of Poland
predecessors.text: the Silesian Province of Bolesław III's testament, held with the Seniorate by Władysław II until 1146

successors.name: Duchy of Legnica
successors.text: Cliopatria's Legnica shape covers Wrocław in 1305-1313

successors.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
successors.text: Cliopatria's Bohemian shape covers Wrocław from 1314

ledger.x: 1138: the Silesian Province is formed under Władysław II.
1146: Władysław II is exiled and Silesia goes to Bolesław IV.
1163: Władysław's sons return to Wrocław.
1172: the brothers partition the duchy, Racibórz to Mieszko.
1172: a strip around Opole goes to Jarosław.
1177: Bolesław returns by Casimir II's mediation and must give Głogów to his brother Konrad.
1190: Głogów returns to Bolesław.
1201: Opole is reunited with Silesia.
Early 1202: Mieszko Tanglefoot takes Opole from Henry the Bearded.
1210: Henry the Bearded takes Lubusz and Gubin.
ledger.cp: Konrad II of Lusatia (Margraviate of Lusatia)

ledger.x: 1218: Lubusz is no longer Henry's.
1229-1230: Henry takes Lubusz again.
1231: Henry the Bearded takes over the regency of Sandomierz for the minor Bolesław V.
1232: Henry the Bearded enters Kraków as High Duke.
Summer 1234: Odonic gives Henry half of Greater Poland.
1234: Henry takes direct control of Opole.
August 1234: the Treaty of Luchani gives Bolesław V Sandomierz.
1238: Henry II the Pious is regent of Sandomierz and Opole-Racibórz.
1239: Henry II gives up the regency of Upper Silesia.
5 June 1239: Władysław Odonic dies and Henry II takes his lands.
9 July 1239: Bolesław V takes over Sandomierz.
1241: Lubusz is granted to Mieszko.
ledger.cp: Duchy of Lubusz (Mieszko, son of Henry II)

ledger.x: 1241: Greater Poland is no longer Silesian.
10 July 1241: Konrad of Masovia enters Kraków.
1242: Lubusz is reintegrated.
ledger.cp: Duchy of Lubusz (Mieszko, son of Henry II)

ledger.x: 1248: Silesia is divided between the brothers.
End of 1277-78: Henry IV Probus pays his ransom in land.
1279: Cliopatria's outline grows to Zielona Góra and the Lubusz Land.
August 1289: Henry IV Probus takes Kraków.
1290-1291: the duchy loses its southern territories.
1290-1291: the Świdnica towns pass to Jawor.
23 June 1290: Henry IV dies and bequeaths Kraków to Przemysł II.
1304: last year of the Cliopatria Silesia shape.

wars.name: Barbarossa's expedition against Poland (1157)
wars.outcome: Bolesław IV the Curly submitted to the emperor and was forced to cede Silesia; Władysław's sons returned in 1163 by the agreement signed at Nuremberg.

wars.name: Revolt of Mieszko Tanglefoot and the partition of 1172
wars.outcome: Mieszko Tanglefoot revolted in 1172; Bolesław I divided Silesia, Racibórz to Mieszko and Opole to Jarosław.

wars.name: Wars of Henry the Bearded with Konrad I of Masovia
wars.outcome: War began in 1228; Konrad captured Henry at Spytkowice in 1229, beat his expedition at Gniezno in 1231 and Henry entered Kraków in 1232; the Treaty of Chełm (1233) confirmed Henry as High Duke and regent of Sandomierz and he gave up Łęczyca and Sieradz.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Poland and Battle of Legnica
wars.outcome: Henry II the Pious was defeated and killed at Legnica on 9 April 1241; all of Lesser Poland fell under Mongol control.

wars.name: Henry IV Probus against Bolesław II and Henry V of Legnica
wars.outcome: Henry IV was seized at Jelcz and imprisoned in 1277, his allies were beaten at Stolec on 24 April 1277, he gave Bolesław II a third of his duchy as ransom; he took Henry V of Legnica, Henry III of Głogów and Przemysł II at Sądowel in February 1281.

wars.name: War for the Kraków succession
wars.outcome: After Leszek the Black's death Henry IV Probus fought at Siewierz on 26 February 1289, took Kraków in August 1289 and held it to his death on 23 June 1290, bequeathing it to Przemysł II.

certainty.note: The Oder basin is described without boundary lines on the pages opened.
